summary: 100-foot Aermotor steel tower with a 7x7 ft cab, built 1937 with the new refuge; still standing behind a gate; registered on the NHLR in 2019.

facts.design: Aermotor 100-foot X-brace open steel tower with a 7 by 7 foot observation cab

access.note: Tower sits behind a gate on the refuge headquarters grounds; only authorized personnel may reach it (2024 visitor report)

facts.agency: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Sacramento National Wildlife Refuge

events.note: Built as part of the project to establish the refuge; some documents call it a fire lookout tower, though it was likely also used for wildlife observation
Refuge established in January 1937 with the purchase of Spalding Ranch; a CCC camp housed up to 200 men at the headquarters area
Site noted as the I-5 Lookout in the 1986 Thornton survey

notes_for_editor: Height 30.5 m is converted from the register's 100 ft tower figure; the register's 97 ft (30 m) is the site elevation and is not the tower height. Access rests on one 2024 trip report, so it is marked restricted at medium confidence. No fire staffing data were found. A Living New Deal page (403 when fetched) says the tower 'still stands today' per a search snippet; it was not read or cited. Fact-check 2026-10-09: the story now says the register places the tower in Glenn County and gives Wikipedia's Glenn and Colusa Counties separately; the 2024 blog post is dated September 2024, and the visit date is not stated in the post.
